summary: I wrote plan.md for a logging camp on a 40 × 34 block clearing beside a rutted road. It has a dark spruce-log bunkhouse with notched corners, a front porch and a stone cook chimney, plus a tall open sawmill (end facing the road, vent on the ridge, brick boiler stack). Both roof specs passed a dry run with no warnings. It reads as a lumber camp because the logs go in from a log pile at the front, pale sawn boards come out to a yard at the back, and the clearing is full of stumps. A dark spruce-log bunkhouse (cobble plinth, notched corners, porch, fieldstone chimney) beside an open pole-frame sawmill with a brick boiler stack, a log deck, lumber stacks and stumps. I appended elements.md (26 items) and the PALETTE, VOCABULARY (33 helpers), ROOMS and PARTS sections to plan.md, leaving the architect's sections and coordinates unchanged. The six parts split along trades: log shell, sawmill frame, roofs, fittings, chimneys and fires, grounds. I did not run any builds, so none of this has been rendered or walk-checked.

Bunkhouse log shell: Bunkhouse shell built in parts/bunkhouse.mjs: plinth ring, saddle-notched spruce log courses y=2..5 with every opening and the hearth cells left as air, plank ground and loft floors with hatch, partition with doorway, porch deck/posts/rails/step, west cordwood. make.sh clean (no refused or off-palette writes from this part).

summary: inspection: Fixed the between-parts problems: make.sh now passes; walk is ok for all six rooms (the loft was unreachable and is now reached 75/75 by a stair up from the mess back row); no indoor dark cells; outdoor dark cells cleared (ground minimum light 1); palette now covers the roof stair/slab blocks.
polish: The plan's loft access is still the ladder at (5,2..4,16) with hatch (5,5,16); it is kept in game, but the walker cannot climb ladders, so the new loft stair (mess back row, 15..17,2..4,16 with the loft floor cut at 15..17,5,16) is the walkable route. The architect should decide whether the stair replaces the ladder: the plan says 'Stairs: none'.

roof-sawmill.json was missing at the top level (roofs.mjs reads it and make.sh died). I wrote it from the plan.md architect spec (slate, verge stripped_spruce_log, gable spruce_planks, no overhang key). The crew/part-3 copy differs (material mix, tuff_brick eave, spruce verge, overhang 1); the choice between them is the architect's.

palette.json: added polished_deepslate_stairs/_slab (roofs) and stripped_spruce_log_stairs (pale_timber), the stair and slab forms the roof tool uses for blocks already listed. This widens the palette; if the palette is meant to stay closed, the roof spec should be changed instead.

Lamp posts added to grounds.mjs at (5,27), (13,31), (22,31), (34,31), (3,3), (34,3) (six, on top of the two planned) to clear the outdoor dark cells; the ground light map now has min 1 but is dim (1-7) in 348 of 942 cells, which is fine for mobs but is not bright.

Porch: the post and stump moved off the window-sill and shutter cells in room-4; the head-level fence moved off the shutter at (8,3,7); the duplicate beam loop in grounds.mjs was removed (roofs.mjs owns the beam). The porch floor cell (15,3,7) is still unreached (verdict ok).

check: 27 orphan flags, 26 are the intended saddle-notch log ends; the other is the spruce_slab at (3,5,7), the bunkhouse roof eave overhang, cosmetic. The sawmill has 5 standable cells unreached (verdict ok); not inspected cell by cell.

waste.what: Worked out by hand why the loft walk failed: the walker needs solid floor under each standing cell and passable headroom at the jump start (cell y+2), and it cannot climb a ladder. I tried a stair and then a mirrored stair, each iteration worked from the walker source.
waste.cost: 2 full build+walk cycles, about 20 cell probes; the mirrored stair needed a second look at the landing, which a bed walled off.
waste.tool: `mcd walk --explain <x,y,z>` (or `--from`/`--to`) that prints the step the walker refused and which rule blocked it (no floor, no headroom at the jump start, ladder not climbable). A `mcd room` suggestion of a stair route with the holes it needs would have made this one step.

waste.what: Read the dark-cell map by eye and converted the zeros to coordinates with awk (the first decode was off by one column).
waste.cost: 3 map reads, 2 lamp rounds (4 posts, then 2 more after the first round left 15 dark cells)
waste.tool: `mcd light build.nbt --y 1 --dark-list` printing each dark cell as x,z, and `--suggest-lamps` giving lamp-post cells that clear them with fence and lantern placement checked against air and the plan's footprints.
